rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: urinary symptoms with danger signs
rule_level_problems.problem: Two of the four Urgent branches are (active_condition "Kidney disease") and (active_condition "Kidney stone"). Descendants match in due_to and 'Chronic kidney disease' is-a 'Kidney disease', so any patient with urinary symptoms and a pre-existing kidney disease (or a previously recorded stone) on their record is marked Urgent, which the page does not say: its trigger is the acute criteria (blood/protein + new swelling/BP/oliguria; blood + sudden severe one-sided pain). This is the house pattern from the briefing, but 'Kidney disease' is a common chronic condition in this population, so the over-trigger is larger here than on most pages. Inlining the criteria, as was done for pyelonephritis, would avoid it.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for urinary infection features / Diagnose probable simple UTI in a woman / Diagnose probable complicated UTI
rule_level_problems.problem: 'Urinary tract problem' is encoded as 'Disorder of urinary system', whose descendants include Kidney disease, Kidney stone, Urinary tract infectious disease, Urethritis, Proteinuria of undiagnosed cause and Hematuria syndrome, i.e. the very conditions this page records. If any of these is on the record as a clinical finding, the Simple UTI rule is suppressed and the Complicated UTI rule fires; the page means a known structural/functional urinary tract problem. A narrower concept (e.g. 'Disorder of urinary tract proper' or a 'Known present' qualifier) would be closer; at minimum this should be noted.

rule_level_problems.problem: Minor concept choices: 'Oliguria' for 'passing little urine' where 'Decreased urine output' (finding) is the closer paraphrase; 'Generalized aches and pains' for 'body pain' where 'Generalized acute body pains' (finding) exists. Neither is wrong. The flow-problem branch (leakage of urine, poor stream/difficulty passing urine) is referral-only with no diagnosis, so its omission is consistent with the no-manage-tasks rule; 'Urinary incontinence' and 'Difficulty passing urine' exist should a later pass want them.

summary: The red box is fully and correctly encoded (all five criteria, right concepts, thresholds and and/or logic), and the woman/man infection branches (simple and complicated UTI, MUS, acute prostatitis, possible diabetes and pregnancy) match the flowchart. The most consequential gap is the entire schistosomiasis branch (blood on dipstick without infection features -> Schistosoma ova -> 'Schistosomiasis likely'), which has no rule although 'Urinary schistosomiasis' exists in SNOMED. Second, the uncomplicated and complicated pyelonephritis rules share one diagnosis concept and the uncomplicated rule has no exclusions, so they are indistinguishable; and the priority rule's active_condition triggers on Kidney disease and Kidney stone will mark patients with pre-existing kidney disease Urgent.
